title.narrative: Multi-Sectoral, Localized Support to Hard-to-reach Communities in Khartoum, Sennar and Al-Jazira states in Sudan

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtAs a continuation of the current SHF Project in hard-to-reach areas, the proposed project titled "Multi-Sectoral, Localized Support to Hard-to-Reach Communities in Khartoum, Sennar, and Al-Jazirah states in Sudan" project is an initiative by the Danish Refugee Council (DRC), in partnership with Sudan Zero Waste Organization (SZWO) in close collaboration with the Mutual Aid Groups (MAGs). It seeks to provide lifesaving assistance to the local communities living in hard-to-reach (H2R) areas across three key states, namely Khartoum, Al-Jazira, and Sennar. As a result of the ongoing conflict since 15 April 2023 between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and Rapid Support Forces (RSF), a large part of these states' population requires multi-sectoral humanitarian assistance. According to the International Organization for Migration’s (IOM) Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) Mobility overview, 33% of the IDPs in the country are originally from Khartoum State, Additionally, approximately 8% of the displaced in the country are residents from Al-Jazira and have respectively fled to Sennar, Gedaref, Kassala and Red Sea State. in Sennar displacement is stated at 3% representing 315,355 IDPs. DRC and its local partner with the involvements of the MAGs have designed the project aimed at maximizing the efficiency of the intervention leveraging their respective sectoral expertise and humanitarian access capacity. The sectors targeted under this project include Protection activities, Wash activities and food support through communal kitchens.ltbrgtThe intervention will aim to address the critical Protection and Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) needs in conflict-affected areas of Khartoum, Sinnar, and Al-Gaziera states in Sudan. The protection component of the project will provide community led emergency protection response services that strengthen the protection environment and improve access to lifesaving protection support. Through support for the establishment and/or ongoing functioning of Women and Girls Safe Spaces access to information, support for psychosocial wellbeing and overall a sense of safety for Women and Girls will be ensured. Similarly, the project aims to support the psychosocial wellbeing and strengthen access to a sense of normalcy for boys and girls (and to a lesser degree their caregivers) through support for the establishment and/or ongoing functioning of Child Friendly Spaces. The project will also facilitate the relocation of at-risk individuals from conflict areas to areas of safety, and support the connection of such individuals to ongoing humanitarian services based on needs in these areas. ltbrgtThis project will also aim to address the critical Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) needs in conflict-affected areas of Khartoum, Sinnar, and Al-Gaziera states in Sudan. It seeks to provide comprehensive WASH interventions to mitigate health risks and promote sustainable hygiene practices in targeted Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) camps and host communities. The initiative is designed to improve access to clean water, proper sanitation facilities, and enhanced waste management systems, focusing on building resilience and reducing the vulnerability of affected populations. Through a participatory approach, the project collaborates with Emergency Response Rooms (ERRs), local stakeholders, and government entities to ensure effective and inclusive service delivery. Key activities include hygiene awareness, latrine construction, water point rehabilitation, waste management, and capacity building for local communities. The project will ensure sustainability through community involvement and empowerment, aiming to create long-term impact in improving public health and well-being.ltbrgtlt/pgt
